quests.instruction: We sing the school song ___ the end of the assembly. Which word fits?
quests.hint: We name the last part of an event.
quests.explanation: 'At the end of' plus an event names its last point: at the end of the film, at the end of the term. 'In the end' means finally, after something has happened.
quests.funFact: 'At the end of the day' is also an expression that means 'when everything is considered'.

quests.instruction: We argued about where to go, but ___ the end we chose the beach. Which word is missing?
quests.hint: The phrase means 'finally, after all the discussion'.
quests.explanation: 'In the end' means finally, after a lot of talking. 'At the end' needs 'of' plus a thing, as in 'at the end of the day'.
quests.funFact: 'In the end' and 'finally' are close in meaning.

quests.instruction: There is a small shop ___ the end of our street. Which word fits?
quests.hint: We name the last point along the street.
quests.explanation: 'At the end of' can also name a place: at the end of the street, at the end of the road. It means the last point along it.
quests.funFact: People often give directions like 'at the end of the road, turn left'.

quests.instruction: Be at the gate ___ eight o'clock, because the coach leaves at 8:05. Which word fits?
quests.hint: You must be there no later than eight.
quests.explanation: 'By eight o'clock' means no later than eight. It is a deadline for arriving. 'Until' would mean something continues up to eight.
quests.funFact: 'By' plus a time almost always shows a deadline.

quests.instruction: The shop will stay open ___ the end of the week, so we have plenty of time. Which word belongs here?
quests.hint: The shop stays open all the way up to that time.
quests.explanation: 'Until the end of the week' means it stays open all the way up to then. 'By' would suggest a deadline for something to happen.
quests.funFact: 'Until' fits things that continue, like stay, wait and keep.

quests.instruction: I'll finish my project ___ the end of the week, so I can hand it in on Monday. Which word fits?
quests.hint: The project must be ready no later than that time.
quests.explanation: 'By the end of the week' is a deadline: the project will be finished no later than then. 'Until' would mean working up to then.
quests.funFact: Deadlines are the last time something can be done.

quests.instruction: Lena arrived at eight o'clock. The lesson began at a quarter past eight. Which sentence is correct?
quests.hint: Compare eight o'clock with a quarter past eight.
quests.explanation: Eight o'clock is earlier than a quarter past eight, so Lena arrived before the lesson. 'After' and 'during' would put her arrival later.
quests.funFact: Being early helps students settle in before lessons start.

quests.instruction: The concert runs from seven until nine o'clock. Sam arrives at eight o'clock. Which sentence is correct?
quests.hint: Eight o'clock falls between seven and nine.
quests.explanation: Eight o'clock is between the start and the end of the concert, so Sam arrived during it. 'Before' and 'after' would be outside those hours.
quests.funFact: Latecomers to concerts usually wait for a pause before they go to their seats.

quests.instruction: The shop closes at six o'clock. Mia arrives at half past six. Which sentence is correct?
quests.hint: Half past six is later than six o'clock.
quests.explanation: Half past six is later than six o'clock, so Mia arrived after closing time. 'Before' would be earlier, and 'until' does not fit an arrival.
quests.funFact: Many shops put the closing time on a sign near the door.

quests.instruction: Our school sports day is ___ the last Friday of June. Which word belongs here?
quests.hint: The last Friday is one particular day.
quests.explanation: 'On' is used for particular days, even when they are described in words: on the last Friday of June, on my birthday.
quests.funFact: We say 'in June' for the month but 'on the last Friday of June' for the day.

quests.instruction: Aunt Rosa's bakery opens ___ dawn, long before anyone else is awake. Which word fits?
quests.hint: Dawn is one exact moment: when the sun begins to rise.
quests.explanation: We use 'at' with moments of the day like dawn, sunrise, sunset, dusk and noon.
quests.funFact: Dawn is when the sun begins to rise, and dusk is when it begins to get dark.

quests.instruction: The new library will open ___ about three weeks, probably around early July. Which word completes the sentence?
quests.hint: She says how long we have to wait until it happens.
quests.explanation: 'In about three weeks' means after about three weeks from now. 'For' shows how long something lasts, and 'during' needs an event.
quests.funFact: 'In' plus a period of time can look into the future: in two days, in a month.

quests.instruction: 'How long will we stay?' 'We will stay ___ Friday, and then we'll drive home.' Which word fits?
quests.hint: They stay for several days, up to Friday.
quests.explanation: 'Until Friday' means they stay all the way up to Friday, and then they leave. 'By' would be a deadline.
quests.funFact: 'Stay until' is a very common pattern in everyday English.

quests.instruction: Which plan for the trip is written correctly?
quests.correctAnswer: We leave on Saturday morning, at seven o'clock, and we return on Sunday evening.
options: We leave in Saturday morning, on seven o'clock, and we return at Sunday evening.
We leave at Saturday morning, in seven o'clock, and we return in Sunday evening.
We leave on Saturday morning, at seven o'clock, and we return on Sunday evening.
quests.hint: Check the day, the clock time and the part of the day.
quests.explanation: 'On Saturday morning', 'at seven o'clock' and 'on Sunday evening' use 'on' for days and 'at' for clock times. The other sentences swap them.
quests.funFact: A day plus a part of the day always takes 'on'.

quests.instruction: Which sentence shows a deadline?
quests.correctAnswer: Hand in your homework by Friday.
options: Hand in your homework by Friday.
quests.hint: A deadline is the last time something can be done.
quests.explanation: 'By Friday' means no later than Friday, which is a deadline. 'Until' shows something continuing, and 'during' shows when something happens.
quests.funFact: 'Deadline' is a word that is also used in newspapers and offices.

quests.instruction: The story about the fox is ___ page 12 of the book. Which word fits?
quests.hint: A page is a flat surface with a number.
quests.explanation: We say 'on page 12' because a page is a surface. We say 'in the book' because the book contains many pages.
quests.funFact: 'In' is for the whole container, and 'on' is for a surface.

quests.instruction: Everyone sat ___ the train, and the guard closed the doors. Which word belongs here?
quests.hint: Think about big public vehicles, where passengers can walk about.
quests.explanation: We say 'on' for large public transport: on a bus, on a train, on a plane. We say 'in' for small vehicles like cars and taxis.
quests.funFact: We also say 'on a bike' and 'on a motorbike'.

quests.instruction: We drove to the beach ___ my uncle's car. Which word fits?
quests.hint: A car is a small vehicle.
quests.explanation: We say 'in a car' and 'in a taxi' because they are small vehicles that we sit inside. 'On' is for buses, trains and planes.
quests.funFact: We can also say 'by car', which means the same without 'the' or 'a'.

quests.instruction: Our plane landed ___ Heathrow Airport, near London. Choose the missing word.
quests.hint: An airport is a stop on a journey.
quests.explanation: We use 'at' for places seen as a stop on a journey: at the airport, at the station, at the bus stop. We use 'in' for cities.
quests.funFact: People say 'in London' but 'at Heathrow Airport'.

quests.instruction: Our plane arrives ___ Dubai at midnight. Which word fits?
quests.hint: Dubai is a city.
quests.explanation: We 'arrive in' a city or a country, and 'arrive at' a smaller place like an airport or a hotel.
quests.funFact: Dubai is a city in the United Arab Emirates, and it has one of the busiest airports in the world.

quests.instruction: Look! There is a fly ___ my soup! Which word belongs here?
quests.hint: Think about something inside a liquid.
quests.explanation: We say 'in' for something inside a liquid or container: in my soup, in the water. 'On my soup' would mean on the surface only.
quests.funFact: 'Waiter, there's a fly in my soup' is a famous old joke.

quests.instruction: Gran is waiting ___ the top of the stairs. Which word belongs here?
quests.hint: We name a point along the stairs.
quests.explanation: We use 'at the top of' or 'at the bottom of' for a point along something like stairs or a hill. 'On top of' is for something placed above another thing.
quests.funFact: We say 'at the top of the stairs' but 'on top of the cupboard'.

quests.instruction: A red cherry sits ___ top of the cake. Which word fits?
quests.hint: The cherry rests above the cake, touching it.
quests.explanation: 'On top of' means placed above and touching the surface. 'At top of' is missing 'the', and 'in top of' is not used.
quests.funFact: 'On top of' also means 'in addition to', as in 'on top of that, it rained'.

quests.instruction: The teacher is standing ___ the front of the class. Choose the missing word.
quests.hint: We name a position in the room.
quests.explanation: We use 'at the front of' or 'at the back of' for a position in a room or a group: at the back of the bus. 'Under' and 'on' do not fit.
quests.funFact: 'In front of' and 'at the front of' are different: 'in front of' means before something; 'at the front of' means in the first part.

quests.instruction: The little cottage is hidden ___ the trees in the forest. Which word makes the sentence correct?
quests.hint: There are many trees, not just two.
quests.explanation: 'Among' is used for three or more things in a group. 'Between' is for two things, so it does not fit a whole forest of trees.
quests.funFact: 'Amid' is a more formal word that is close in meaning to 'among'.

quests.instruction: The ball rolled ___ the two goalposts and into the net. Which word is missing?
quests.hint: There are exactly two goalposts.
quests.explanation: 'Between' is used for exactly two things, and the ball passes through the gap. 'Among' needs three or more things.
quests.funFact: 'Between' can also be used for two sides, such as 'between you and me'.

quests.instruction: Mia sat ___ her friends in the circle. There were six of them. Which preposition fits?
quests.hint: Six people are more than two.
quests.explanation: 'Among' is used for a group of three or more. Six friends make a group, so Mia sat among them. 'Between' would need exactly two.
quests.funFact: A circle is a good shape for talking because everyone can see each other.

quests.instruction: Who is sitting ___ you on the bus? Which word fits?
quests.hint: One spelling means 'next to', and the other means 'in addition to'.
quests.explanation: 'Beside' means next to. 'Besides' means as well as or in addition to. 'Between' would need two people, one on each side.
quests.funFact: 'Beside' has no 's' at the end, just like the word 'side'.

quests.instruction: ___ pizza, we are having salad and fruit for lunch. Which word fits?
quests.hint: We have pizza and other things as well.
quests.explanation: 'Besides' means in addition to: besides pizza, we have salad and fruit. 'Beside' would mean next to the pizza.
quests.funFact: 'Besides' can also start a sentence on its own: 'Besides, it is raining.'

quests.instruction: Which sentence says that three friends came in addition to me?
quests.correctAnswer: Besides me, three friends came to the party.
options: Beside me, three friends came to the party.
Between me, three friends came to the party.
Besides me, three friends came to the party.
quests.hint: In addition to me means 'as well as me'.
quests.explanation: 'Besides me' means 'as well as me', so there were four people in total. 'Beside me' would mean next to me, and 'between me' needs two things.
quests.funFact: A single extra 's' changes 'beside' into 'besides' and changes the meaning.
